entries.question: 2. Test for the commutative property of union and intersection of the sets P = { x : x is a real number between 2 and 7} and Q = { x : x is a rational number between 2 and 7}.
steps: Write P = {x ∈ ℝ : 2 < x < 7} and Q = {x ∈ ℚ : 2 < x < 7}. Both inequalities are strict, so the endpoints are excluded.
Every rational number is real, hence Q ⊆ P. But not every real number in this interval is rational; for example √10 belongs to P but not Q.
Therefore P ∪ Q = P. Reversing the operands, Q ∪ P = P. Thus P ∪ Q = Q ∪ P.
Because Q ⊆ P, P ∩ Q = Q. Likewise Q ∩ P = Q. Hence P ∩ Q = Q ∩ P.
Both union and intersection satisfy the commutative property for the given sets. Check: 3 belongs to both sets, while √10 belongs only to P; neither 2 nor 7 belongs to either set.
entries.answer: P ∪ Q = Q ∪ P = P = (2, 7); P ∩ Q = Q ∩ P = Q = ℚ ∩ (2, 7). Both properties are verified.
